author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged BRICS members to take a peacemaking role in the Middle East war during an address to the bloc’s leaders in New Delhi on Saturday. Xi said the conflict does not serve the international community and that China would work with other members on efforts aimed at peace.

The appeal came as BRICS leaders tried to bridge divisions between Iran and the United Arab Emirates, both members of the expanded group but positioned differently in the regional conflict. Their summit agenda includes diplomacy, economic cooperation and the bloc’s effort to increase the influence of emerging and developing nations in global institutions.

Xi also said China will take over the BRICS chairmanship in 2027 and host the organization’s 19th summit. The group now includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the UAE. Xi’s remarks do not establish a peace process on their own, but they signal that Middle East diplomacy has become a central test of whether the expanded bloc can coordinate across competing national interests. Further summit statements and bilateral meetings are expected as the gathering continues.
dek: The Chinese president called for a peace role as the expanded bloc navigates differences between Iran and the United Arab Emirates.
headline: Xi urges BRICS to pursue peacemaking role in Middle East war
